1.question: [System] In which year did the Alsace Grand Cru classification finally reach 51 sites, and what was the last site delimited?
1.explanation: The first 25 in 1983 and a further 25 in 1992 (50 in total), then in 2007 the 51st Grand Cru "Kaefferkopf" (Ammerschwihr) was formally delimited, and it is also the only Grand Cru that has allowed blending since its creation.
2.question: [Geology] In Claude Sittler's geological classification, which family has only one member, Kastelberg?
2.explanation: Kastelberg (Andlau) is the only schist Grand Cru in all Alsace — Silurian Steige schist metamorphosed by the neighbouring granite into hard, dark rock, in a class of its own among the ten geological families.
3.question: [Geology] Which Grand Cru is the only site in all Alsace made of true volcanic rock?
3.explanation: Rangen (Thann & Vieux-Thann) is the only true volcanic site in all Alsace (siliceous rock and basaltic lava) and also the southernmost Grand Cru; Thann is also the only town whose entire territory is classified as Grand Cru.
4.question: [Size] Which of the following Grand Crus is the largest?
4.explanation: Schlossberg (Kientzheim) covers 80.28 ha, the largest of the 51 Grand Crus; by contrast Kanzlerberg (Bergheim) covers only 3.23 ha and is the smallest Grand Cru.
5.question: [Blending Exceptions] Which two Grand Crus allow several varieties to be blended?
5.explanation: Altenberg de Bergheim (Riesling 50–70% + Pinot Gris 10–25% + Gewurztraminer 10–25%) and Kaefferkopf (Gewurztraminer 60–80% + Riesling 10–40% + Pinot Gris ≤30%) are the only two Alsace Grand Crus that allow blending.
6.question: [Variety Exception] Which Grand Cru is historically the only site authorised to plant Sylvaner?
6.explanation: Zotzenberg (Mittelbergheim) has historically been known for Sylvaner, and is the site where Sylvaner was specially authorised at Grand Cru level — unique within the whole Grand Cru system, which is "in principle limited to the four noble varieties".
7.question: [History] The earliest known written record of wine in Alsace (589, Merovingian era) took place at the location of which Grand Cru?
7.explanation: According to Grégoire de Tours, in 589 the Merovingian king Childebert II owned vineyards at Marlenheim — the earliest known written record of wine in Alsace, and Marlenheim is exactly where the limestone Grand Cru "Steinklotz" lies.
8.question: [Variety Tendency] Which site is called the "roof of the Alsace vineyards", where Gewurztraminer shows extreme power?
8.explanation: Zinnkoepflé (Soultzmatt & Westhalten) reaches 420 m and, shielded by the mountains, is one of the driest areas in all Alsace — the representative site where Gewurztraminer, the "king of Alsace wines", shows power and spice.
9.question: [Special Area] How far is the Cléebourg area from the main Alsace vineyard belt, forming an isolated enclave?
9.explanation: Cléebourg was historically part of a continuous belt of vine growing; in the first half of the 20th century the belt was cut, leaving Cléebourg about 90 km from the main Alsace vineyard belt as an isolated enclave in the north.
10.question: [Special AOC] Klevener de Heiligenstein is the non-aromatic variant of which variety? What is distinctive about its authorised area?
10.options.0: A variant of Riesling, which can be planted throughout Alsace
10.options.1: The non-aromatic variant of Gewurztraminer (Savagnin rose), which may be planted only in a few villages around Heiligenstein
10.options.2: A variant of Pinot Gris, planted only in Andlau
10.options.3: A variant of Muscat, planted only in Ribeauvillé
10.explanation: Klevener de Heiligenstein is the non-aromatic variant of Gewurztraminer (Savagnin rose), introduced to Heiligenstein in 1742. It is a complementary geographical indication within AOC Alsace with Savagnin rose as the only authorised variety, limited to the immediately neighbouring villages of Bourgheim, Gertwiller, Goxwiller, Heiligenstein and Obernai.
11.question: [Clos] Which estate exclusively owns Clos Sainte Hune, and for which variety is it known?
11.explanation: Clos Sainte Hune (Hunawihr, 1.67 ha) is exclusively owned by the F.E. Trimbach estate, 100% Riesling, one of the most esteemed Rieslings in Alsace and the world, regarded as the peak representative of Alsace Riesling.
12.message: 🎉 Congratulations on completing the Level 2 Comprehensive Assessment! You have travelled through all 51 Grand Crus and the most distinctive corners of Alsace!
12.keyPoints.0: ✅ Grand Cru classification: created in 1975, three waves of delimitation in 1983 / 1992 / 2007 reaching 51 sites
12.keyPoints.1: ✅ Ten geological families: from schist (1) to marl-limestone (13), spanning hundreds of millions of years of geological history
12.keyPoints.2: ✅ Two blending exceptions: Altenberg de Bergheim and Kaefferkopf
12.keyPoints.3: ✅ Special areas: the Cléebourg enclave and the Klevener de Heiligenstein complementary geographical indication
12.keyPoints.4: ✅ Famous Clos: legendary plots such as Sainte Hune, Windsbuhl and Zahnacker
